feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is valid and is iteration 7 (best raced, 125.3) with one change: base_speed 1.3 to 1.15. Sensors (five 12 mm footprints at x = -0.02 to +0.02, y = 0.03), weights, kp 3.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.35, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12 and last_direction are all held, so any change in result should come from speed. Nothing is obviously broken.

The evidence supports testing speed. Every design so far (iterations 0 to 9) has ended off_track on every trial, with max_error at 0.060 to 0.068 and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. Iteration 7 is the only design with oval progress above 0.5 at 1.3 and has line loss of 1.0 on s-bend. Iteration 3 showed that lower speed with higher ki reduced drift slightly. Iterations 8 and 9 both moved away from iteration 7 and scored lower, so the controller and sensing at iteration 7 are the best current base. Centrifugal drift at bends scales with speed squared, so a small speed cut is a plausible way to keep the robot inside the 0.06 m band.

The risk is progress. Iteration 6 at base 1.2 reached only 0.49 on oval, and the course needs about 1.5 m/s to finish, so a cut to 1.15 may lower progress and the 250 times progress term with it, even if line loss falls. The race will show whether that trade is worth it. Approving is right here: the change is clean, the base is the best raced, and there is one iteration left after this, so telemetry from this race is worth more than a revision made without it.

What to change next depends on the race. If line_loss_events fall to 1 or fewer on oval and s-bend and max_error drops below 0.06, but oval progress falls below about 0.5, raise base_speed toward 1.3 to 1.4 in steps. If max_error still reaches 0.06 with line loss unchanged, speed is not the limit: keep 1.3 and raise kp alone toward 3.5 with the 12 mm footprint and wheel_track 0.12 held, since iteration 8's kp change was confounded with the track change. If the score falls below iteration 7 (125.3) with no drop in line loss, return to base_speed 1.3 for the final iteration.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events are 1 or fewer on oval and s-bend but oval progress falls below about 0.5, raise base_speed in steps toward 1.3 to 1.4, since iteration 7 at 1.3 reached 0.61 oval progress and iteration 6 at 1.2 reached only 0.49.

If max_error still reaches 0.06 with line loss unchanged at base_speed 1.15, revert base_speed to 1.3 and raise kp alone from 3.0 toward 3.5 with sensor_size 0.012 and wheel_track 0.12 held, because iteration 8's kp 3.5 result was confounded with the 0.11 m track.

If the score falls below iteration 7 (125.3) with no drop in line_loss_events, revert base_speed to 1.3 for the final iteration, since iteration 7 is the best raced design and speed is the only variable changed here.
